summary: This program builds a small list of farmers' market products, prints the whole inventory, then uses a stream pipeline to pull out the names of the organic summer items in price order. The result is a List<String> of just the names.

lines.text: The filtering work lives in its own method, so main stays readable and the pipeline can be reused with any list of products. The method's return type, List<String>, is the promise that only names come back.
Calling stream() on the list opens the pipeline: each product will be handed through the operations that follow. The list itself is never modified.

The lambda is the rule for keeping a product: organic, and a season that mentions summer. The null check has to come before toLowerCase(), or a product with no season set would crash the pipeline — and testing contains("summer") rather than equality is what lets "Late Summer" through.
Comparator.comparingDouble builds the ordering rule from a single field, and MarketProduct::getPrice is a method reference — shorthand for the lambda p -> p.getPrice().

This is where the stream changes type: a stream of MarketProduct becomes a stream of String. Mapping after filtering and sorting matters, because both of those steps need the full object and its price.
collect is the terminal operation, and nothing above it actually ran until this line was reached. It gathers the surviving names into the List<String> the method returns.
